title: Designing Null-Safe APIs
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of designing null-safe apis using at least one correct term from the lesson.

Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Designing Null-Safe APIs** as part of **Null Safety and Type Handling**. Kotlin distinguishes nullable types such as `String?` from non-null types such as `String`; callers must handle the nullable case explicitly. Use the subtopics—Nullable Parameters and Return Values, Representing Missing Data, Avoiding Unnecessary Assertions—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Functions, null safety, strings, and collections are the building blocks of most practical Kotlin code. Choosing the right operation reduces avoidable errors and makes behavior easier to test.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Kotlin distinguishes nullable types such as `String?` from non-null types such as `String`; callers must handle the nullable case explicitly.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with nullable parameters and return values. Then compare it with representing missing data. Identify the input, state, dependency, or branch that determines the result. The snippet is a static reference for CodeLeaf and is not executed in the lesson page.

items.title: Nullable Parameters and Return Values
items.text: Nullable Parameters and Return Values is about representing or handling the possibility that a value is absent. Keep nullability visible in the type and choose an explicit fallback, branch, or result model rather than assuming the value exists.

items.title: Representing Missing Data
items.text: Representing Missing Data is about representing or handling the possibility that a value is absent. Keep nullability visible in the type and choose an explicit fallback, branch, or result model rather than assuming the value exists.

items.title: Avoiding Unnecessary Assertions
items.text: Avoiding Unnecessary Assertions helps make behavior observable and repeatable. Define the expected result, include a boundary or failure case, and preserve enough diagnostic information to locate the cause without leaking sensitive data.

content_blocks.code:
data class ApiResult<T>(val value: T?, val error: String? = null)

fun main() = println(ApiResult(value = "ready"))

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: The compiler can guarantee that a Java platform value never contains null.
